author: allnes
title: CachingTest TearDown fails - file locked by another process on Windows runner
signature: remove_all: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process|Flaky Test

failed_jobs.name: C++ unit tests / C++ unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: CachingTest TearDown throws C++ exception: remove_all file locked by another process

key_errors: unknown file: error: C++ exception with description "remove_all: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.: \"12690347162626515821_12196_4036_10864143409testCache\"" thrown in TearDown().
root_cause: During TearDown of a CachingTest variant, std::filesystem::remove_all attempted to delete the test cache directory on Windows, but another process (likely the OpenVINO runtime/plugin still holding the cache file open from the previous test step) had the file locked. This is a Windows-only file-locking race condition in the test teardown, unrelated to the PR changes (GPU clang-tidy updates). The test is classified as Flaky Test because it reflects a timing/OS race rather than a code logic error introduced by the PR.
reproduction_steps: Run CachingTest/CachingTest.TestLoadChangeCacheDirOneCore_by_device_name_supports_cache_dir/ByRemoteContext_testCache on a Windows machine with active process that holds cache files open.
recommended_actions: Retry the failed CI job - the file-lock race is transient and typically resolves on retry.
Investigate the CachingTest TearDown to add retry logic or delay when remove_all fails with a file-lock error on Windows.
Consider using unique temp dirs per test process to reduce file-lock contention.
prevention_strategies: Add retry logic in CachingTest TearDown for Windows when remove_all fails with ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION. Use ScopedTempDir or equivalent RAII wrappers that handle Windows file-lock races gracefully.
historical_context: No prior occurrence of this exact pattern found in the investigation database. Windows file-lock issues in test TearDown are a known source of intermittent failures on Windows CI runners.
